entries.name: Regeneration
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id, kind and trigger kept verbatim per naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies (g.sustain existingFamilies) and atom-family-library.md §3.3 (`resource.delta`, `OnTimer`, cat S). ssot-sockets.md:573 and ssot-reroll.md:550 both cite `atom.regeneration.tN` as `resource.delta, OnTimer` with no `element` param and no `variants` block, so this stays a single-row family the same way `lifesteal` does on the on-hit side. `nameWords.suffix` reuses the shipped band-A/B/C word table verbatim from ssot-affixes.md:756 ("of Knitting" / "of Renewal" / "of the Wellspring"). `roles` is the sustain column of ssot-affixes.md §4.3's role x group matrix, translated from the stale 12-role table to core.v1.json's 15 ids: head-protective->head-guard, core-protective->core-guard, mantle-utility->mantle, girdle-resource->girdle, jewel-minor->jewel-minor-a and jewel-minor-b, footing/jewel-major/armament-secondary stay. sense-utility, manipulator-offense and armament-primary carry weight 0 in that column and are correctly absent; the commander-only `standard` row carries weight 2 there but is deliberately excluded the same way the on-hit and on-death files exclude it — it is not one of the 15 body roles. Every entry in this file shares this identical roles list, same precedent as those two sibling files.

entries.name: Cleansing
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to cleanse a harmful status when struck
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. `kindId: status.clear` per atom-family-library.md §3.5 (cat U, "strip statuses on trigger") and naming.v1.json's g.sustain existingFamilies. `status.clear`'s AllowsTrigger list (AtomKindRegistry.cs) is the event set only — OnSpawn/OnDamageDealt/OnDamageTaken/OnDeath, no OnTimer — so a periodic cleanse is not constructible, and `OnDamageTaken` is the trigger that reads as a defensive rider (strip what's wearing you down each time you're hit), paired with `mantle`'s equip-slot description in ssot-equip-slots.md:89 ("elemental mitigation... and status cleansing. The resistance home."). No shipped word table exists for this family in ssot-affixes.md's illustrative sample, so `nameWords` is minted here following the same suffix `of-construct` grammar the shipped `regeneration`/`warded` tables use. `target` and `statusId` are declared in status.clear's ParamSchema but left out of `params` here the same way `amount` is left out of every resource.delta entry — the generator resolves which status(es) a cleanse rider strips, this file only fixes the trigger.

entries.name: Warded
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id, kind and element-variant expansion kept verbatim per naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies and ssot-item-categories.md:85 ("one carries `atom.regeneration` and the other carries `atom.warded`"). ssot-affixes.md's own draw example (row 3, §7.1) and ssot-sets.md:575 both cite `atom.warded.<element>.tN` as `shield.grant, OnSpawn` — that fixes the trigger even though atom-family-library.md §3.5's sketch says "on hit or spawn" more loosely; the two committed worked citations agree on `OnSpawn`, so this file keeps that reading rather than inventing a second on-hit trigger for the same family. `amount`, `sourceClass`, `priority`, `durationTicks` and `refillOnMerge` are all in shield.grant's ParamSchema and all left out of `params` for the same reason `amount` is absent everywhere else in this corpus — they are generated or defaulted, not authored per entry.

entries.name: Renewing Husk
entries.notes: NEW family minted on this group's reserved `sust` stem (naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies), word `husk` — a mechanical description (a shell that keeps re-forming), not a flavour adjective. `shield.grant` declares AllTriggers (AtomKindRegistry.cs), so `OnTimer` is legal there the same way it already is on `resource.delta`; this is the periodic-grant counterpart to `warded`'s one-shot `OnSpawn` grant, and a genuinely different mechanic from `shield_regen` in `g.shield-stat` (which raises an EXISTING shield's regen rate as a `stat.derived` modifier, not a discrete fresh grant on a cycle). `powerBand: low` because a repeating grant compounds over a fight the way a single `warded` grant does not, the same reasoning `volley`/`husk`'s own on-death cousins use for repeatable riders sitting beside a one-shot sibling. Plant reading: the bark keeps closing over the wound. Zombie reading: the husk keeps patching itself back together — one mechanic, the two fictions the brief asks for.

entries.name: Callusing
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `sust`, word `callus` (tissue that thickens exactly where it is repeatedly damaged — mechanical, not a theme adjective). Reactive shield-on-being-struck is a distinct cell from every shipped or already-minted family in this group: `warded` grants once on `OnSpawn`, `sust-husk` grants on a fixed `OnTimer` cadence, and this one grants only in response to being hit — closer in shape to `retribution`/`hit-mend` (both `OnDamageTaken`) but on the shield attach point instead of the resource one, so it composes differently against the actor's other defences rather than adding another number to the same HP pool. `powerBand: low` for the same reason `sust-husk` sits there: a conditional, repeatable proc is kept modest relative to `warded`'s single deliberate grant.

entries.name: Fresh Graft
entries.displayTemplate: cleanse all harmful statuses on spawn
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `sust`, word `freshgraft`. `status.clear`'s allowed trigger set is the event set (OnSpawn/OnDamageDealt/OnDamageTaken/OnDeath, no OnTimer per AtomKindRegistry.cs), and `OnSpawn` fills the one cell `cleansing` (`OnDamageTaken`) leaves open — a self-cleanse the instant the wearer takes the field, rather than a reactive one during the fight. Plant reading: a new graft carries none of the old plant's rot. Zombie reading: rising again sheds whatever wore the last body down. `tags: ["utility"]` matches `cleansing`'s own choice and atom-family-library.md §3.5's `U` category for this kind.

entries.name: Grit
entries.displayTemplate: {value}% chance to cleanse a harmful status when you land a hit
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `sust`, word `grit` (a mechanical description of pushing through, not a theme adjective). Fills the last open `status.clear` x event-trigger cell this file has a use for: `cleansing` is `OnDamageTaken`, `sust-freshgraft` is `OnSpawn`, and this is `OnDamageDealt` — self-cleanse from the act of attacking rather than from being hit or from spawning. This is the family the brief's 'a zombie refuses to stop' fiction fits most directly: the attack itself burns off whatever is slowing it down. Distinct from `sust-freshgraft` (one-shot, at spawn) and from `cleansing` (reactive, on being struck) by trigger alone, the same way this group's other new families are distinguished from their siblings by trigger rather than by a numeric field.
